items.note: The hovered first card in the 4-column grid only gets a pale gray fill on its text area. It doesn't move and has no hard offset shadow, so it sits flush with the grid like every other card. The linked-card lift is still missing, the same as in rc.2.
In dark mode the hovered card's body only gets a slightly darker charcoal fill. The card stays in place with no 35%-white offset shadow, so it is hard to tell which card is under the pointer.

On a touch screen the single-column grid correctly shows no lift, as the hover guard intends. The first card shows the subtle-gray body fill, and the yellow band, scrolling pill strip and pink price tags look right.

A raised toast with an ink border and the hard offset shadow sits at the bottom left. It says 'Added 1 item (…) to your cart' with an underlined View cart link and an outlined close button, and the header cart count changes to a pink 1, so the result and the next step are both clear.

The same bottom-left toast on a charcoal raised surface with a light border and a light offset shadow. The text and View cart link are readable, and the paper-filled selected Color pill and the pink Add to cart are the only loud elements.
The toast spans the bottom of the 390px screen with its hard shadow, message, View cart link and close button. It sits under the stacked product content without covering the Add to cart button.

Under a periwinkle band, the checkout card shows the summary 'Fix 3 fields to place your order' with an icon. Each empty field has a red border and an icon plus a message below it, and the focused Full name field keeps its red border inside the ink focus outline. Place order is the one pink action.

Same layout in dark mode: red-bordered fields and icon-led messages read clearly on the charcoal card, and the focused field shows a pink halo with the error border still showing. Nothing is hidden or low-contrast.
The Items and Checkout cards stack in one column. The error summary, the three red-bordered fields with their messages and the pink Place order button all fit at 390px, and nothing is clipped.
Focus is on the Cart nav pill, which shows a thick ink outline that follows the pill shape next to the ink-filled current Shop pill. It is clearly visible and in the system's language.
The focused Cart pill gets a pink ring next to the paper-filled current Shop pill on the dark header. It is easy to see and the rest of the grid is unchanged.
On mobile the Cart pill under the brand row shows the same ink focus outline beside the ink-filled Shop pill, and the band and grid below look correct.

All 11 placeholders are now different sticker objects for their own items: tote, backpack, duffel, tee, pocket tee, chore coat, mug, skillet, folded towels, key ring and beanie. Each is drawn from basic shapes with a heavy ink outline, filled with pink, band and raised colors, slightly tilted, on varied band squares. This fixes rc.2's generic image glyph, and the grid now has the colorful, varied feel of the reference's product wall.
The detail image is a large tilted white tote with a pink label, a heavy ink outline and an arched handle on a yellow square. It reads clearly as a bag and is built to the sticker recipe.

A periwinkle garment with a white crew collar and a hem band on yellow. The outlines are clean, but it has short sleeves and reads as a t-shirt, almost the same silhouette as the pocket-tee sticker in the grid.
The cart's sticker is a pink coin with a heavy ink plus glyph and a yellow extruded rim, slightly tilted on paper. It matches the coin recipe and the reference's coin stickers at small size.

findings.summary: Linked product cards still don't lift on hover. The hovered card only gets a faint body fill, with no -4px translate and no hard offset shadow, in light or dark mode. The linked-card lift is a signature element, and rc.2 already flagged it.
findings.promptFix: A hover state for a linked card is the lift and nothing else. Don't use a fill change in its place. The card's outer bordered box (the anchor or the element that receives the pointer) translates -4px -4px and shows shadow.md in color.shadow.hard. If a background tint is added, it comes with the lift, never instead of it. Before reporting, hover one card in each theme and confirm its position and shadow have changed; a color change alone fails the check.

findings.summary: The sweater sticker has short sleeves and almost the same silhouette as the t-shirt sticker, so it reads as a t-shirt. Two related items look like one drawing in two colors.
